practice-17:
North, South, East and West are the four accepted answers in this site's current question bank. Enter one full direction, rather than all four together. The prompt asks for a member of a set, so a single correct choice is enough. Northeast and southwest are useful directions too, but they belong to a different group from the four main directions requested here.

This guide covers our independent game. The same wording on another trivia website may use a different answer list or scoring system. The answer review saved with your completed dive is the right reference for the points awarded in that particular run.

Read “four main” as the important restriction

The key task is to distinguish a cardinal direction from an intermediate direction. North, east, south and west form the cardinal set. Northeast lies between north and east, while southwest lies between south and west. Those combined names provide more detail, but more detail does not make them better answers to this specific question.

A useful test is to picture a simple compass rose with just four labels. Start at the top with north, then move clockwise through east, south and west. If the answer you are considering needs a position between two of those labels, it is outside the set requested by this prompt. That quick picture is usually more useful than searching for an unusual word.

A map exercise that makes the distinction practical

Imagine a small map with a library in the centre, a park directly above it, a station directly below it, a school to its right and a museum to its left. If the map is drawn with north at the top, the park is north of the library, the station is south, the school is east and the museum is west.

Now place a café above and to the right of the library. Its position is northeast. That would answer a question asking for an intermediate compass direction, but it would not answer our current four-direction prompt. The exercise shows why a geographically meaningful response can still fail an exact category condition.

The phrase “north at the top” matters. A map can be rotated, and a diagram should identify its orientation before you infer direction from the page. The trivia question avoids that complication by asking for a direction name, not the direction of an object on an unidentified map.

Why left, right, up and down are different answers

Left and right depend on which way a person is facing. If you turn around, your left side changes relative to the room. Cardinal directions describe orientation independently of that turn. A doorway does not become a different compass direction from a table just because you turn your chair.

Up and down can describe vertical movement, positions on a page or a screen layout. Neither word is a substitute for north or south in this answer bank. Similarly, “toward the station” may be a perfectly useful instruction in conversation, but it does not name one of the four requested directions.

This is a recurring trivia skill. Identify the kind of answer the prompt requests before choosing an example. A direction name, a landmark and a relative instruction might all help someone navigate, yet they are not interchangeable answer types.

What to type in this game

Use North, South, East or West. Capitalization does not affect matching. The current bank does not configure N, S, E or W as aliases for this prompt, so the full word is the safest input. An abbreviation that appears on a compass is not automatically a supported game alias.

Enter only one answer. Writing “north or east” introduces extra text and does not ask the matcher to select whichever part it recognizes. If you make a spelling mistake and receive a proposed correction, inspect the suggestion and submit again to confirm it before the timer expires. A displayed suggestion alone is not a scored answer.

Prepared points are not a geography fact

The fallback bank assigns North to Plankton, South to Schooler, East to Rare and West to One in a Krillion. With the configured tier values, those fallback entries correspond to 10, 30, 60 and 100 points. These are game settings, not evidence that one direction is intrinsically harder or less important.

New runs can use observed choices once a prompt has enough eligible browser choices under the scoring rules. A saved run keeps its own scoring snapshot. Consequently, do not use a static guide as a promise that West must always receive the same points in every future dive. Check the run's review when you want to understand an awarded score.

Try these checks before your next dive

First, decide whether “southeast” belongs to the requested four. It does not: it combines two cardinal names. Next, decide whether “west” remains a cardinal direction if a map is rotated. It does; rotating the page changes its appearance, not the category of the word. Finally, decide whether the letter W is a guaranteed accepted submission. It is a conventional label, but this bank does not list it as an alias.

When the question appears in a timed dive, you only need one full direction you can spell confidently. Practising the distinction is useful beyond this easy example: restrictive words such as “main,” “standard,” “classic” and “land” often determine the answer set in other prompts.

Learn more and keep practising

For background on the four-direction set, see National Geographic's Compass reference. The map and typing exercises above are written for this guide; the game's configured answers and tiers come from our own bank.

games-expanded-10:
Electric Company and Water Works are the accepted answers in this site's current bank. The question asks for one utility, so either complete name is enough. Reading, Pennsylvania, B. & O. and Short Line are railroads rather than utilities; a familiar purchasable space is not necessarily a member of the requested category.

The word “classic” also limits the question. Monopoly has many editions, and a property name remembered from a themed or international board may not answer a question about the classic US board. Our guide explains the answer scope for this independent trivia game, rather than claiming to cover every Monopoly product.

Find the property category before recalling a name

A useful way to approach this prompt is to separate the board's kinds of spaces. A street property, a railroad, a utility and a card-drawing space have different roles. Trying to recall every square at once creates unnecessary competition between names. Start with the category “utility,” then retrieve one of the two names in the answer set.

For this question, the utility names refer to electricity and water. That connection provides a short memory cue: think of services supplied to a town rather than transport routes or a coloured street group. Once you have remembered Electric Company or Water Works, stop searching and enter the name clearly.

This cue is for recalling board names. It does not imply that every real-world public service has a corresponding square on the classic board. “Gas company,” “internet provider” and “telephone company” might sound plausible, but plausibility alone is not evidence that a name appears in the specified edition.

Why the edition restriction matters

An answer can come from a genuine Monopoly game and still be outside this prompt. Hasbro's announcement for the Here & Now: The World Edition describes Wind Energy and Solar Energy replacing the traditional utilities. That is a useful example of why the edition qualifier is part of the question, rather than optional background.

If you remember a special board, ask two questions before submitting: does the prompt name that edition, and is the remembered space a utility in the requested version? In our current classic US question, the accepted set remains Electric Company and Water Works. Do not substitute the renewable-energy names merely because they are official names in another product.

There is no need to decide which edition is more familiar or more interesting. The trivia task is to answer the edition actually named. The same principle applies to prompts about a standard deck, a particular sports award or a specified country's version of a game.

Full names, aliases and unsupported shorthand

Electric Company is the full accepted entry. The bank also explicitly accepts “electric” as an alias for that entry. Water Works is the other full entry, and its stored record currently has no additional aliases. Use Water Works rather than assuming that “water,” “water company” or another shorthand will be recognized.

Matching normalizes capitalization and other presentation differences. However, normalization does not turn any related description into an accepted synonym. An alias is a prepared alternative associated with an entry, not permission to invent a new label. A complete printed name is usually the least ambiguous input when you already know it.

Type one entry rather than “Electric Company and Water Works.” The latter explains the whole answer set to a human reader but is not a request for the game to select one name. If the timer is running, clarity is more useful than a sentence describing what you remember.

A sorting exercise for common mix-ups

Consider these candidate answers: Water Works, Reading Railroad, Chance, Electric Company and Boardwalk. Sort them by the question's category before thinking about rarity. Water Works and Electric Company fit the accepted utility set. Reading Railroad belongs to the railroad category. Chance is not a utility name, and Boardwalk is a street property.

Now try “Solar Energy.” This candidate requires a different check: it is associated with a different edition, so it fails the version restriction here. The first exercise catches category mistakes; the second catches edition mistakes. Both can produce a rejected answer, but the reasoning behind the rejection is different.

You can use that distinction after a game too. If you missed this prompt, ask whether you forgot the two names, confused property types or remembered a different board. Each problem suggests a more useful practice task than simply memorizing the highest-scoring entry.

How points work for this prompt

In the prepared fallback bank, Electric Company is Plankton and Water Works is One in a Krillion. Those tiers correspond to 10 and 100 points. This distribution is an editorial game setting; it is not a published survey of Monopoly players or a claim about how often each board space is visited.

Once a prompt has enough eligible browser choices, new runs can use observed-frequency scoring under this site's rules. Existing runs retain their saved tiers. Your completed-dive review therefore takes precedence when checking what a submitted answer earned. The name of a utility and its score are separate pieces of information: the board category establishes validity, while the run snapshot determines points.

Sources and your next practice step

Hasbro's World Edition announcement identifies the traditional utility names and illustrates an edition change. For a physical board's rules, use the instructions supplied for that particular product. This page is an independent answer guide and does not imply affiliation with Hasbro.

Explore the games collection for other prompts where a version or piece category matters. Read the answer help and scoring rules, or start a mixed dive. Unlimited does not provide a guaranteed Monopoly-only question set.
geography-expanded-12:
China and Russia are the two accepted answers in this site's current question bank. Choose one country name. Mongolia is landlocked between those neighbours; the question is about sharing a land boundary, rather than being nearby, belonging to the same broad region or having a historical connection.

This is an answer guide for our independent trivia bank. A country may be relevant to a discussion of Mongolia without satisfying this particular border condition. Understanding that distinction is more useful than trying to name the most distant country you can associate with the region.

Treat “land border” as a precise relationship

The central check is whether the two countries' territories meet along a land boundary. Being on the same continent does not establish that relationship. Nor does a flight route, trade agreement or cultural connection. Those facts can link two places without making them neighbours in the sense required here.

For this prompt, reduce the task to a small set: Mongolia, the named country, and the boundary between them. China fits, and Russia fits. Japan and South Korea do not become correct because they are familiar East Asian countries. A broad regional association is only a starting point for recall, not the final test.

This distinction also prevents a common timed-trivia habit: seeing a place name and submitting the first nearby country that comes to mind. Pause long enough to identify the relationship requested. A question about a border is different from one about a continent, a capital or a neighbouring region.

A simple map picture to remember

Picture Mongolia between Russia to the north and China to the south. This is a memory aid for the two-country answer set, not a detailed description of every turn in either boundary. You do not need border lengths, coordinates or crossing names to answer the current question.

If you practise with a map, first find Mongolia's outline and then follow its perimeter. Record each country that meets that outline. This is more reliable than looking at a large region and estimating which labels seem close. A map's scale can make gaps and narrow areas hard to notice, so zoom in before treating apparent proximity as contact.

After that exercise, cover the labels and recall the two names. The objective is to make the relationship memorable without adding facts the prompt does not request. When the timer starts, one correctly recalled neighbour is sufficient.

Nearby places and historical names can distract

A candidate can be geographically close but still fail the shared-boundary test. If you are uncertain about another country in the region, return to the outline exercise rather than extending the answer set from memory. “Near Mongolia” and “has a land border with Mongolia” are different statements.

Historical maps introduce another kind of confusion. The question names Mongolia in an ordinary present-day geography context, not the maximum territory of a historical empire. A country associated with Mongolian history is not automatically a present-day land neighbour. Unless the wording specifies a historical period, do not substitute a historical political map for the modern country relationship.

Inner Mongolia is also a possible source of category confusion: it is not a separate country to submit as Mongolia's neighbour. The requested answer type is a country name. The two prepared entries are China and Russia, so use one of those names directly rather than a regional label.

What the matching engine expects

Enter China or Russia. The stored records for this prompt do not configure additional aliases. Full descriptive alternatives such as a country's formal state name should not be assumed to work merely because they refer to the same place. The short canonical names are the clearest choices for this bank.

Capitalization is normalized, so ordinary lower-case typing is fine. Entering both countries together is a different issue: the game expects one prepared answer, not a list that it will split into separate guesses. A short sentence such as “it borders China” also adds unnecessary text when the accepted entry is simply China.

If a typing error produces a suggested correction, confirm the suggested answer with a second submission before time expires. If an entry is rejected, you can try another while the round remains open. Rejection tells you that the input did not match the run's configured entries; it is not, by itself, a general geographical proof about the world.

Fallback scores and saved runs

In the prepared bank, China uses Plankton and Russia uses One in a Krillion. The configured fallback scores are therefore 10 and 100 points. These values are part of this game's scoring design, not statements about country size, boundary length or the difficulty of geography as a subject.

New runs may use observed choices once the prompt meets the site's sampling requirement. A started run keeps its scoring snapshot, so a guide showing fallback values cannot guarantee the points in every later dive. Use the answer review attached to your completed run when checking an award. Keep factual eligibility and score calculation separate: one determines whether a country fits, the other determines the game's reward.

Check your understanding with three questions

First, would a nearby country qualify merely because it appears next to Mongolia's name on a small map? No; the territories must share a land boundary. Second, does a historical connection make a country a current neighbour? No; the time frame and relationship still matter. Third, must you name both accepted countries? No; this prompt asks for one example.

For background, the World Bank's Mongolia country framework describes Mongolia's landlocked position between Russia and China. This guide adds exercises for reading the trivia condition; it does not reproduce that report's economic analysis.

Continue with the geography collection, all prompt guides or the rules. A new Unlimited dive mixes subjects and does not guarantee this exact border question.
